heading.en: Why is a car safe in lightning?

hook.en: During a thunderstorm, one of the safest places outdoors is inside a closed car. Its metal body keeps the electric field out. This is electrostatic shielding.
hook.kn: ಗುಡುಗು ಸಿಡಿಲಿನ ವೇಳೆ ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಕಾರಿನೊಳಗೆ ಇರುವುದು ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಸುರಕ್ಷಿತ. ಅದರ ಲೋಹದ ದೇಹವು ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವನ್ನು ಒಳಗೆ ಬಿಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಇದೇ ಸ್ಥಾಯಿವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಕವಚನ.

title.en: List the electrostatic properties of a conductor.
Explain how a dielectric is polarised and reduces the field.

say.en: During a thunderstorm, one of the safest places outdoors is inside a closed car. Its metal body keeps the electric field out. This is electrostatic shielding. In this lesson: List the electrostatic properties of a conductor.
Explain how a dielectric is polarised and reduces the field.

body.en: In electrostatic equilibrium: (1) E = 0 everywhere inside a conductor; (2) the whole conductor is at one potential; (3) any excess charge sits on the outer surface; (4) just outside, E is normal to the surface with magnitude $\sigma/\varepsilon_0$; (5) the field inside an empty cavity in a conductor is zero, whatever happens outside: electrostatic shielding.
body.kn: ವಾಹಕದ ಒಳಗೆ E = 0, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇಡೀ ವಾಹಕ ಒಂದೇ ವಿಭವದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಆವೇಶ ಹೊರ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ; ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯ ಹೊರಗೆ E = σ/ε₀, ಲಂಬವಾಗಿ. ವಾಹಕದ ಒಳಗಿನ ಪೊಳ್ಳು ಹೊರಗಿನ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಿಂದ ಕವಚಿತವಾಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: conductors and dielectrics

narration.en: Put a conductor in a field: free electrons shift until the field inside is exactly zero. Excess charge sits only on the surface, and the field just outside is σ/ε₀, normal to the surface. A dielectric slab in a field is polarised: bound charges on its faces oppose the applied field. So the field inside falls to E₀ divided by K, the dielectric constant of the material. Example: with E₀ = 3 × 10⁵ V/m and K = 5, the field inside is 6 × 10⁴ V/m.

Put a conductor in a field: free electrons shift until the field inside is exactly zero. Excess charge sits only on the surface, and the field just outside is sigma divided by epsilon 0, normal to the surface. A dielectric slab in a field is polarised: bound charges on its faces oppose the applied field. So the field inside falls to E 0 divided by K, the dielectric constant of the material. Example: with E 0 equals 3 times 10 to the power 5 volts per metre and K equals 5, the field inside is 6 times 10 to the power 4 volts per metre.

With the battery removed first, Q stays fixed and V and E drop to 1/K. Either way C = K C0. Plates: 0.01 m², 1 mm apart.

body.en: A dielectric (insulator) has no free charges. In an external field its molecules become dipoles: non-polar molecules (O₂, H₂, CO₂) get induced dipoles, polar molecules (H₂O, HCl) line up. The dipole moment per unit volume is the *polarisation* P. Bound surface charges appear and reduce the field inside to $E_0/K$, where K, the dielectric constant (relative permittivity), equals ε/ε₀.
body.kn: ಪರಾವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ವಸ್ತುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮುಕ್ತ ಆವೇಶಗಳಿಲ್ಲ. ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಣುಗಳು ದ್ವಿಧ್ರುವಗಳಾಗಿ ಸಾಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ (ಧ್ರುವೀಕರಣ). ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಬದ್ಧ ಆವೇಶಗಳು ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವನ್ನು E₀/K ಗೆ ಇಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Non-polar: induced dipoles; polar: dipoles line up

tagline.en: Electrostatics of conductors and electrostatic shielding, polar and non-polar dielectrics and polarisation, capacitance, the parallel-plate capacitor and the effect of a dielectric.

myth.en: Doubling the charge on a capacitor doubles its capacitance, since C = Q/V.

truth.en: Doubling Q doubles V, so C = Q/V stays the same. Capacitance is fixed by A, d and K only. C = Q/V looks like it depends on Q, the same way R = V/I seems to depend on current. Both are ratios that stay constant because the numerator and denominator change together.

say.en: In a conductor in electrostatics: $E = 0$ inside, excess charge on the surface, $V$ constant, $E = \sigma/\varepsilon_0$ just outside and normal to it.
A charge-free cavity in a conductor is shielded from outside fields.
Dielectrics are polarised by a field (induced or aligned dipoles) and reduce the field inside them by the factor K.
$C = Q/V$; parallel plates: $C = \varepsilon_0 A/d$, rising to $K\varepsilon_0 A/d$ with a dielectric.
Slab of thickness $t$: $C = \varepsilon_0 A/(d - t + t/K)$; metal slab: $\varepsilon_0 A/(d - t)$.

goal.en: Electrostatics of conductors and electrostatic shielding, polar and non-polar dielectrics and polarisation, capacitance, the parallel-plate capacitor and the effect of a dielectric.

explain.en: Non-polar molecules get only an induced dipole in a field. Polar molecules already have one and are partly aligned by the field. Both reduce the field inside the dielectric.

takeaway.en: In a conductor in electrostatics: $E = 0$ inside, excess charge on the surface, $V$ constant, $E = \sigma/\varepsilon_0$ just outside and normal to it.

narration.en: Many people think: Doubling the charge on a capacitor doubles its capacitance, since C = Q/V. Actually: Doubling Q doubles V, so C = Q/V stays the same. Capacitance is fixed by A, d and K only. C = Q/V looks like it depends on Q, the same way R = V/I seems to depend on current. Both are ratios that stay constant because the numerator and denominator change together.

problem.en: A conducting sphere of radius 10 cm carries 2 nC. Find the potential at its surface and at its centre, and the field just outside and at the centre.

steps.en: Inside a conductor V is the same everywhere: 180 V at the centre, and E = 0 there.
Just outside: E = kq/R² = 18 / 0.01 = 1800 N C⁻¹.

answer.en: V = 180 V at the surface and the centre; E = 1800 N C⁻¹ just outside, 0 at the centre

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A conducting sphere of radius 10 cm carries 2 nC. Find the potential at its surface and at its centre, and the field just outside and at the centre.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A conducting sphere of radius 10 centimetres carries 2 nC. Find the potential at its surface and at its centre, and the field just outside and at the centre.
Surface: V equals kq over R equals 9 times 10 to the power 9 times 2 times 10 to the power minus 9 divided by 0.1 equals 180 volts.
Inside a conductor V is the same everywhere: 180 volts at the centre, and E equals 0 there.
Just outside: E equals kq over R squared equals 18 divided by 0.01 equals 1800 newtons C to the power minus 1.
So the answer is V equals 180 volts at the surface and the centre; E equals 1800 newtons C to the power minus 1 just outside, 0 at the centre.

problem.en: The field between two plates in air is 2 × 10⁵ V m⁻¹ (charge kept fixed). A slab of dielectric constant 5 fills the gap. Find the field inside the slab.

steps.en: The free charge is fixed, so E = E₀/K.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. The field between two plates in air is 2 × 10⁵ V m⁻¹ (charge kept fixed). A slab of dielectric constant 5 fills the gap. Find the field inside the slab.

say.en: Let us solve this together. The field between two plates in air is 2 times 10 to the power 5 volts m to the power minus 1 charge kept fixed. A slab of dielectric constant 5 fills the gap. Find the field inside the slab.
The free charge is fixed, so E equals E 0 over K.
E equals 2 times 10 to the power 5 divided by 5.
E equals 4 times 10 to the power 4 volts m to the power minus 1.
So the answer is 4 times 10 to the power 4 volts m to the power minus 1.

say.kn: ಪರಾವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ವಸ್ತು ಧ್ರುವೀಕರಣಗೊಂಡು ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವನ್ನು E 0 over K ಗೆ ಇಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.
